lines: Spyglass author M.G. Siegler and host Alex Kantrowitz discuss how the AI data center boom is driving up memory costs and squeezing Apple's margins, turning Apple from a component price-setter into a price taker even as it stays out of the AI spending race.
The show notes Apple's services revenue growth is slowing, so the company needs new ways to monetize beyond its existing ecosystem.
They see the folding 'iPhone Duo' as a push into premium, high-margin hardware, and a possible sign that foldables, working as a compact phone and a larger screen, eventually replace the glass slab.
AI wearables that passively record and summarize conversations, like Amazon's listening bracelet, are framed as 'gaslight insurance' but face serious privacy, consent and legal hurdles.
They argue AI is becoming the interface itself: models generating widgets and tools on the fly from user intent could make static, pre-built apps obsolete.
title: Storm Clouds Ahead For Apple?, Debating Amazon’s Bee Frontier, AI as UI
